original_question: In a sub-Riemannian manifold, optimal singular curves starting from a fixed point q_0 are known to fill a nowhere dense subset of the manifold. Can the set filled by such optimal singular curves nevertheless have positive measure?
target_in_paper: Section III, "Morse–Sard theorem" for the endpoint maps, specifically the final unnumbered open question asking whether the subset of M filled by optimal singular curves starting from q0 can have positive measure. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the sub-Riemannian setting, fixes a base point q0, restricts to optimal singular curves, recalls the known nowhere-dense conclusion, and asks exactly the narrower positive-measure question stated at the end of Section III. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
missing_details: The paper formulates the issue through the endpoint map on the H^1-Hilbert manifold of admissible paths starting at q0; singular curves are the critical points of that map. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

"Optimal" should be made explicit as "length minimizing," which is the paper's parenthetical clarification. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

What is meant in context by curves "filling" a subset of M is the subset of endpoints reached from q0 by such curves, since Section III is about critical values of the endpoint map. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

The nearby broader problem in the paper is different: whether all singular curves starting from q0 can fill the whole manifold M. Your refined version should not merge that broader question with the narrower one about optimal singular curves and positive measure. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

No additional hypotheses such as genericity, analyticity, rank, or dimension restrictions are stated in this particular question, so the refined version should not add any. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
refined_question: Let M be a smooth sub-Riemannian manifold and fix q0 in M. Consider the endpoint map from the H^1-Hilbert manifold of admissible paths gamma:[0,1]->M with gamma(0)=q0 to M, gamma->gamma(1), and call its critical points singular curves. It is known that the subset of M reached from q0 by optimal (i.e. length-minimizing) singular curves is nowhere dense. Can this subset nevertheless have positive measure in M? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
justification: This is the exact unnumbered open question stated at the end of Section III, not one of the numbered conjectures or propositions elsewhere in the paper. The draft is already close; the main sharpening is to anchor "singular curve" to the endpoint-map framework and to clarify that the set under discussion is the subset of M obtained as endpoints of length-minimizing singular curves starting at q0. The sentence immediately above it raises a broader question about all singular curves filling all of M, but that is not the same problem and should not replace the narrower target. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
